niche.habitat: 10-12 km depth, ice-ocean boundary, fissure zones

body: Armored carapace, drill-like rostrum, pressure-resistant shell

links: Precise acoustic resonance breaks brittle ice

skill.effect: The creature vibrates its beak to shatter nearby ice and armor plating, leaving cracked surfaces that can be easily cleared.

chains.weakness: Vibration exposes their position to predators

journal.en: They speak in cracks, and the ice answers.

plausibility.summary: Limit Ice Shatter to fissure brine channels, warm ice-ocean interface rinds, and competitor carapace; add enzymatic or abrasive rostrum wear plus vibration as fatigue assist. Keep haunting 'cracks' at ceiling-scale fissures, not arbitrary megabarriers.

analogues.organism: Pistol shrimp cavitation snaps (localized shock) and woodpecker impact drilling—localized material failure, not bulk ice-sheet breaching.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

skill.effect: The creature's frost-resistant hide glistens as it moves through freezing conditions without slowing or stumbling.

chains.weakness: Thermal insulation traps metabolic heat in warm zones

journal.en: Frost clings to the world, but not them.

plausibility.summary: F16 already posits antifreeze glycoproteins at ~275 K; strong selection at the ice-ocean boundary and in fissure seeps. Overheating in warm vent pockets fits insulating cuticle trade-offs.

skill.effect: The creature draws in vent vapors through its spiracles, converting the gases into a sudden burst of speed that carries it swiftly for a short while.

chains.weakness: Cannot metabolize oxygen or nitrate efficiently

chains.trait: Radial arms anchor to uneven ice
links: High gravity demands low center of mass
Planetary mass compresses interior and surface

skill.effect: The creature's radial arms anchor deeply into the ice, locking it firmly in place so it cannot be pushed or dragged away.

chains.weakness: Requires solid surface to plant arms; fails in water

journal.en: They fight gravity with every joint.

plausibility.summary: 1.53 g (F4) favors low center of mass and adhesive anchoring on solid substrata; ice ceiling/Fissure-wall gripping at the interface is a credible opposite solution to mid-water Velaescura. Fails in open water is consistent.

secrets: Their spiracles can temporarily reverse flow to inject vent gases into rival carapaces.
Antifreeze proteins double as electrical insulators, allowing them to ride micro-currents near ice.
moments: A fissure groans open, bleeding warm vapor into the cold. Cortezón climbs the steam like a pilgrim, shell drinking the heat.

journal.en: They speak in cracks, and the ice answers.
Gravity is not an enemy; it is an anchor.
